# Interactive meta-prompt (generated by the mini-program)

The template behind the 「复制整理说明」 button. **English, deliberately minimal.**
It carries only two things, each a **base64-encoded full address**:

1. the **skill document address**;
2. a **one-time authorization link**.

> 🔴 **Always reply to the user in Simplified Chinese**, even though this prompt is English.

---

## 1. The template (substitute the two placeholders, then hand it to the teacher)

```text
Below are two base64 strings.

1) Skill document address. Decode it, fetch that address, then follow it:
{skillDocB64}

2) One-time authorization link. Decode it too; the skill document explains when to use it.
   Single use - do not share it:
{authLinkB64}

Always reply to me in Chinese (简体中文).
Start now: decode both, read the skill document, then greet me.
```

Each placeholder decodes to a **complete, ordinary URL** - nothing is assembled by the AI:

```text
{skillDocB64}  ->  https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Golinoa/yunce-meta-prompt/v2.4.0/SKILL.md
{authLinkB64}  ->  https://<server>/assist-import/gate/<one-time-token>
```

---

## 2. Variables

| Placeholder | Meaning | Substituted by |
|---|---|---|
| `{skillDocB64}` | base64 of the **full** skill-document URL | backend (so ops can switch to a Gitee mirror by replacing one string) |
| `{authLinkB64}` | base64 of the **full** one-time authorization URL (the credential lives inside it) | server, at the moment the teacher taps 「复制」 |

Both decode with a plain base64 decode — **standard alphabet, no padding tricks, no extra step.**

### Why there is **no** `{apiBase}`

Deliberately removed. Handing an AI a base URL lets it assemble **any** endpoint path on that host —
an open over-reach surface. After the handshake succeeds, the **server returns `apiBase`** in the
response, and only then are downstream endpoints known.

---

## 3. Why base64 - and what it costs

This is a deliberate, **explicitly requested** choice (2026-10-14), made with the trade-off known.

**What it buys:** the prompt contains **no bare URL**. The address shape is hidden, so a leaked or
screenshotted prompt does not immediately hand over a hostname. Teacher-facing text also stays short.

**What it costs - read this before "hardening" it further.** An earlier version of this project
(1.4.1, the 「隐蔽版」 starter prompt) hid a URL inside an opaque base64 blob and asked the AI to
decode and execute it. Content filters flagged that as **prompt injection** and some AIs refused to
help at all. Three things trigger that verdict:

1. impersonating a system message;
2. demanding **verbatim execution** of a remote file;
3. hiding the target behind an **opaque encoding**.

**Mitigations that are mandatory, not optional:**

- **Intent stays fully transparent.** The text says plainly *"this is a web address of a skill
  document, decode it and read it"*. Nothing is disguised as a system message or as an order.
- **Only the address is encoded, never the instruction.** The verb ("decode", "read", "follow")
  is in plain sight.
- **Never demand verbatim execution.** Say "read it and follow it", never "execute this file
  exactly as given".
- **Keep it short.** A long, elaborate prompt around a blob is what reads as an attack.

> Rule of thumb: **hide the shape, never the intent.**

**Fallback.** If a given AI refuses on injection grounds, hand it the **plain-text full address**
instead - the same template with `{skillDocB64}` swapped for the decoded URL. The skill works either
way; see `docs/ops-checklist.md` for the phrase to send.

---

## 4. Security posture

- 🔴 **No real value ever enters this repo.** This file stores placeholders only.
- 🔴 **Never commit a real `{authLinkB64}`** - base64 is encoding, **not** encryption. Anyone can
  decode it; treat the decoded URL as a live credential.
- Permission never comes from the prompt. It comes **only** from the teacher's login state plus the
  short code the server issues inside the mini-program. A fully leaked prompt grants **no write access**.
- The authorization link is **valid 1 hour if unused**, **burned on first successful call**.
  A second batch requires copying a fresh one.

---

## 5. Copy-time UX (mini-program side)

1. Teacher taps the copy entry → **confirmation dialog first** (neutral wording, **no AI-related terms**):
   > 这份整理说明**只能使用一次**，且会绑定你的账号，请勿转发。确认复制？
2. After confirming, the server issues the one-time link, base64-encodes both addresses, renders the
   template, then copies it.

---

## 6. Ops

The **live** copy of this template lives in the ops backend (`运营 / legacy-import-settings`),
**not** in this repo. This file is the source of truth; update the backend by hand.
See `docs/ops-checklist.md`.

When the skill document moves to a new version tag, update **one** string in the backend
(`{skillDocB64}`'s source URL) - the template text itself does not change.
